body:
## Problem

`aucmd_prepbuf`, `win_execute_before`, `switch_win` all are similar yet slightly different implementations of a very delicate yet extremely important concept.

ref https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/7257

## Solution

Fix vim's brain damage. Unify the "context switch" impl in `context.c`.

interested parties may be @luukvbaal @barrettruth @zeertzjq @bfredl @seandewar 

## TODO (future followup)

- [ ] update `dev_arch.txt`.
- [x] ctx_win_prep's internal suppressions (block_autocmds, p_acd=false, RedrawingDisabled++)  duplicate the CtxSwitchFlags concepts, but prep must stay self-contained while buffer callers  default to flags=0. https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40674
- [x] win_enter() in prep vs. the core's bare `curwin =` assignment — different enter semantics  (prevwin, enter protocol). https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40674
- [x] The three curwin-restore variants (plain, firstwin-fallback + entering_window + prompt,
  new_curbuf b_nwindows dance) could share a util, but each has different not-found behavior. prevwin restore stays buffer-only for the same reason. https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40667

comment_data.body: `cs_target_curpos` sounds like the position that the cursor should be moved to. Maybe `cs_target_win_curpos` is better?

+#pragma once

+#include "nvim/pos_defs.h"
+#include "nvim/types_defs.h"
+
+typedef struct {
+  String regs;     ///< Registers.
+  String jumps;    ///< Jumplist.
+  String bufs;     ///< Buffer list.
+  String gvars;    ///< Global variables.
+  Array funcs;              ///< Functions.
+} Context;
+typedef kvec_t(Context) ContextVec;
+
+#define CONTEXT_INIT (Context) { \
+  .regs = STRING_INIT, \
+  .jumps = STRING_INIT, \
+  .bufs = STRING_INIT, \
+  .gvars = STRING_INIT, \
+  .funcs = ARRAY_DICT_INIT, \
+}
+
+typedef enum {
+  kCtxRegs = 1,       ///< Registers
+  kCtxJumps = 2,      ///< Jumplist
+  kCtxBufs = 4,       ///< Buffer list
+  kCtxGVars = 8,      ///< Global variables
+  kCtxSFuncs = 16,    ///< Script functions
+  kCtxFuncs = 32,     ///< Functions
+} CtxStateFlags;
+
+/// Temporary, hidden window (fka "autocmd window"): a pooled window created to temporarily show
+/// a buffer that has no window (ctx_switch() on a buffer target), to handle the side effects.  When
+/// switches nest we may need more than one.
+typedef struct {
+  win_T *cw_win;   ///< The window, or NULL if not yet allocated.
+  bool cw_used;    ///< Not currently in use.
+} CtxWin;
+
+/// Flags for ctx_switch().
+typedef enum {
+  /// Don't affect the display (no redraw; limits access to another tabpage).
+  kCtxNoDisplay = 1,
+  /// Block autocommands until ctx_restore().
+  kCtxNoEvents = 2,
+  /// Undo any chdir caused by the switch ('autochdir', win/tab-local CWD) on ctx_restore().
+  kCtxKeepCwd = 4,
+  /// Validate cursor/Visual around the switch; update display (statusline) if the target window's
+  /// cursor moved.
+  kCtxValidate = 8,
+} CtxSwitchFlags;
+
+/// What ctx_switch() switched (set internally).
+enum {
+  kCtxSwitchNone = 0,  ///< zero-initialized: ctx_restore() is a no-op
+  kCtxSwitchWin,       ///< window target
+  kCtxSwitchBuf,       ///< buffer target
+};
+
+/// Context before a temporary switch of current window/buffer. Undone by ctx_restore().
+typedef struct {
+  CtxSwitchFlags cs_flags;              ///< kCtx* flags of the switch
+  int cs_mode;                    ///< kCtxSwitch* (what was switched)
+  // Saved location:
+  handle_T cs_curwin_handle;      ///< saved curwin
+  handle_T cs_prevwin_handle;     ///< saved prevwin (ctx_switch())
+  tabpage_T *cs_curtab;           ///< saved curtab (NULL: tabpage unchanged)
+  bool cs_same_win;               ///< VIsual_active was not reset
+  bool cs_visual_active;          ///< saved VIsual_active
+  int cs_prompt_insert;           ///< saved b_prompt_insert
+  // Temporary location (ctx_switch()):
+  handle_T cs_new_curwin_handle;  ///< ID of new curwin
+  bufref_T cs_new_curbuf;         ///< new curbuf
+  int cs_ctxwin_idx;              ///< autocmd window in ctx_win[], or -1
+  // Target tracking (kCtxValidate):
+  handle_T cs_target_win_handle;  ///< the window switched to
+  pos_T cs_target_curpos;         ///< its cursor before the switch

comment_data.body: Hmm, actually as long as `buf != NULL`, `wp` is always valid here, as it comes from the loop above, and there is no code that may invalidate it. I wonder if this should be made obvious, as Nvim's code relies on `aucmd_prepbuf()` never failing (unlike in Vim where there is a check for `aucmd_prepbuf()` failure every time it is used).

comment_regular_data.body: very nice callout. any problem with heap-allocating CWD string? it actually is an improvement vs the old `win_execute_T` logic, because it usually isn't needed.
I think it's OK. Also, `win_execute_before()`, `win_execute_after()` and `win_execute_T` are Nvim-only stuff. They are the decomposition of Vim's `f_win_execute()` function and don't exist in Vim.
